extracted.intended_audience: health insurance issuers, State regulators, agents/brokers/web-brokers, actuaries, data scientists, HHS/CMS reviewers, and other Marketplace stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed HHS/CMS rulemaking for the Health Insurance Marketplace that specifies certification requirements (QIS), payment/collection processes, MLR adjustment procedures, PRA information-collection reporting requirements, marketing/consent standards, and related operational and burden-estimate details; solicits public comment on these proposals and associated assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Improvement Strategy (QIS) certification requirement (§156.1130)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §156.1130(a), an issuer participating in an Exchange for two or more consecutive years must implement and report on a QIS, including a payment structure that provides increased reimbursement or other market-based incentives in accordance with the health care topic areas in section 1311(g)(1) of the Affordable Care Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute identifies five topic areas (improving health outcomes, preventing readmissions, improving patient safety/reducing medical errors, promoting wellness/health, and reducing health and health care disparities). The proposal would modify prior guidance to allow QHP issuers to submit QISs addressing any two of the five topic areas (rather than mandating specific areas like disparities). Issuers may select quality measures (e.g., Marketplace Quality Rating System measures) or other performance targets based on programmatic goals and enrollee needs. HHS seeks comment on this increased flexibility and on whether issuers should still be required to address disparities specifically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Netting of civil monetary penalties (CMPs) into integrated payment/collections cycle (§156.1215)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to amend §156.1215(b) and (c) to apply the netting provisions of HHS' integrated monthly payment and collections process to CMPs assessed against health insurance issuers and their affiliates, and to base determination of debt on amounts owed after HHS nets amounts owed by the Federal Government under these programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose described: evolve payment/collections with program needs, ensure stability/consistency, improve recovery of Federal debts by withholding funds payable to (or held for) issuers, limit number of back-and-forth charges, mitigate additional collection steps, and prevent inappropriate enrichment of issuers. HHS seeks comment on these changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical cross-reference correction for administrative appeals (§156.1220(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to correct a cross-reference in §156.1220(b)(1) from paragraph (a)(5) to (a)(6) to accurately reflect the scope of review of the reconsideration decision in the administrative-appeals process (reconsideration, then informal hearing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a technical correction to ensure the regulation text correctly references the reconsideration decision's scope; HHS requests comments on the correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-requested MLR adjustment criteria and process (subpart C of part 158)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 2718(b) of the PHS Act and subpart C (including §§158.310–158.346), a State may request adjustment of the individual-market MLR standard if it demonstrates a reasonable likelihood that the 80% MLR standard would destabilize its individual market. The adjustment may be granted for up to a specified period, and the request must include specified information and be assessed under criteria in §158.330.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpart C specifies initiation (§158.310), potential grant duration (§158.311), required supporting information (§§158.320, 158.321), HHS criteria for determination (§158.330), public comment invitation (§158.342), optional State public hearings (§158.343), and reconsideration procedures (§158.346). HHS seeks comment on the effect of the Federal MLR standard on market stability, whether to allow HHS to adjust Federal MLR in States without a State-initiated request, how to determine adjustment magnitude, consultation and publication practices, and whether to modify §§158.311, 158.321, and 158.330 to reduce State burdens (e.g., allowing 5-year adjustments instead of 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability of proposed rule provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS states intent that the various provisions in the proposed rule be severable, so that if any provision is held invalid or unenforceable, other provisions will continue to give maximum legal effect unless the holding is one of utter invalidity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS invites comment on the severability of these provisions. The preamble outlines that multiple distinct programs and provisions are addressed independently (e.g., risk adjustment parameters, user fees, CMP administration, APTC eligibility limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) public comment solicitation topics
rubrics_metrics.description: For any collection of information submitted to OMB, HHS must solicit public comment on: (1) the need for the information collection and its usefulness in carrying out agency functions; (2) the accuracy of burden estimates, including methodology and assumptions; (3) the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected; and (4) recommendations to minimize burden, including automated collection techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS is soliciting comments on these specific issues for the ICRs described in the document and notes that fair evaluation of information collections requires comments on these elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage and time-valuation methodology for burden estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS uses Bureau of Labor Statistics data to derive labor costs and applies a 100 percent increase to wages to account for fringe benefits and overhead. HHS proposes adopting an hourly value of time based on after-tax wages for unpaid activities, starting with weekly usual earnings ($1,206), dividing by 40 to get pre-tax hourly wage (~$30.15), then adjusting by an effective tax rate (~17%) to yield a post-tax hourly wage (~$25.02).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS acknowledges the 100% adjustment is a rough method but believes doubling the hourly wage reasonably estimates total cost; HHS seeks comment on these burden estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rate filing justification (URRT/Actuarial Memorandum) and CSR reporting requirements (§154.215 and §156.430(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuers must submit a rate filing justification consisting of (1) the URRT, (2) a written description justifying any premium rate increase, and (3) an Actuarial Memorandum (as applicable). Proposed change: issuers must report actual CSR amounts paid on behalf of eligible enrollees, amounts previously generated by any CSR load factors, projected CSR amounts, and plan-level CSR load factors calculated using the standard methodology in §156.430(c)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS proposes the URRT contain numerical CSR values (experience-period actual CSR amount, amount previously generated by load factors, projection-period expected CSR amount, plan-level CSR load factor, and expected load-generated amount). The Actuarial Memorandum should explain the methodology used to determine the load factor and compare expected load revenue to expected CSR payments. HHS seeks comments and describes an assumed standard methodology for calculating these values; it also estimates implementation burdens to perform a claim-level re-adjudication to produce required values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation burden estimates for claim-level re-adjudication (one-time and ongoing)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS estimates issuer burden hours and roles to implement claim-level re-adjudication and produce CSR-required values: one-time implementation (per issuer) of 11,400 hours across actuaries, data scientists, programmers, claims specialists, and a project manager; ongoing annual updates of 5,700 hours per issuer for targeted updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS provides role-by-role hour and hourly-rate breakdowns (e.g., Actuaries 2,400 hours at $120.94/hr, Data Scientists 3,000 hours at $108.26/hr, etc.) and total cost estimates per issuer and for all issuers. HHS notes some issuers may have lower or higher costs depending on existing systems and claim volumes and seeks comment on these assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: URRT submission operational burden estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed operational requirement for issuers to enter CSR-related data elements into the URRT (actual CSR paid, amount generated by load factors, expected CSR amounts, CSR load factor, expected amount generated by load factor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS estimates 0.5 hours per plan for Actuaries to collect and enter these data elements (approximately $60 per plan), assumes ~7 plans per issuer with CSR load factors (3.6 hours and ~$430 per issuer), and provides totals across all issuers. HHS requests comment on these estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actuarial Memorandum content requirement regarding CSR load factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuers must include in the Actuarial Memorandum an explanation of the methodology used to determine the CSR load factor and an explanation comparing expected revenue from the load factor to expected CSR payments on behalf of enrollees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS estimates this will require 2 hours per plan for Actuaries to develop and draft the required explanations and add them to the Actuarial Memorandum, with cost estimates per plan, per issuer, and aggregate. HHS seeks comment on the burden estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal review burden estimate for URRT/Actuarial Memoranda
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS estimates Federal Government review costs for URRT and actuarial memoranda related to CSR reporting: GS-14 staff (hourly rate given) requiring estimated hours per plan to review submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, HHS estimates GS-14 level staff at 6 hours per plan to review materials, resulting in aggregate hour and cost estimates. HHS is presenting these estimates as part of the PRA submission and solicits comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandated use of HHS-approved consumer consent form (§155.220(j)(2)(ii)(A) and (j)(2)(iii)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to require agents, brokers, and web-brokers to use an HHS-approved and -created consumer consent form to meet eligibility application review documentation requirements and consumer consent documentation requirements, replacing broader current allowances and clarifying what actions constitute 'taking an action.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: reduce confusion, ensure objective standards, improve HHS investigative ability. The form can be submitted electronically (no printing/mailing costs). HHS estimates approximately 10 minutes (0.17 hours) per enrollment to obtain consumer affirmation using the form and provides national enrollment and cost estimates; HHS seeks comment on these burden estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing conduct standards and advertising/documentation requests (§155.220(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed new standards of conduct prohibiting agents, brokers, and web-brokers from engaging in misleading marketing and requiring them to provide marketing materials to HHS upon request. New §155.220(j)(3)(iii) and (j)(3)(iv) detail prohibitions and HHS' authority to request advertisements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS expects most enforcement contacts to be Technical Assistance (requiring removal of ads) and some Notices of Intent to Terminate (NoITs) requiring confirmation of removal and a review of guidelines. HHS estimates about 70 notifications annually (2/3 TA, 1/3 NoITs), with ~24 requiring documentation submissions and estimates 1 hour per response for removal/review plus cost estimates. HHS seeks comment on assumptions and burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Exchange Enhanced Direct Enrollment (SBE-EDE) blueprint revision ICR
rubrics_metrics.description: States electing to implement the SBE-EDE option must revise their Exchange Blueprint to notify HHS and describe updated processes and controls to manage SBE-EDE implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS believes Blueprint revisions will be nominal in cost (input via CMS web interface), notes that the burden related to the Exchange Blueprint is already approved under an existing OMB control number, and requests comments on the burden associated with this activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed limitation of APTC eligibility to 'eligible noncitizens' (ICR/BHP review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal language (introduced in preamble) would disallow APTC for individuals ineligible for Medicaid due to immigration status and having income below 100% FPL after specified dates, limit APTC eligibility among certain aliens, and extend related SEP removals; relevant ICRs would be submitted for BHP OMB review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble outlines the proposed changes as part of broader rule provisions; HHS is seeking comment on these proposals and will submit associated information-collection requirements for OMB review where applicable.
